sourceNote: Original Evia practice questions mapped to course criteria. These are not official awarding-body or end-point-assessment questions.

questions.prompt: Before starting unfamiliar bricklaying work, which information should be checked first?
options: Only the delivery ticket
The risk assessment, method statement and current drawings
The previous gang's timesheet
Only the weather forecast
questions.explanation: The safe method and current job information must be understood before work begins.

questions.prompt: A task will create respirable silica dust while cutting masonry. What is the best control approach?
options: Work faster so exposure is shorter
Use suitable dust suppression or extraction and the specified face-fit-tested RPE
Wear ordinary glasses only
Cut indoors so dust cannot spread
questions.explanation: Engineering controls should reduce the dust at source, with suitable RPE used as specified.

questions.prompt: What should happen before changing a disc on a masonry saw?
options: Leave the tool running slowly
Disconnect or isolate the power and follow the manufacturer's procedure
Cool the disc with mortar
Remove the guard for easier access
questions.explanation: Isolation prevents accidental start-up while the disc is being changed.

questions.prompt: Which action best protects surface water during bricklaying?
options: Wash wet mortar into a drain
Contain washout and dispose of it using the site procedure
Dilute wash water until it looks clear
Leave washout beside the kerb
questions.explanation: Cementitious washout must be contained so it cannot pollute drains or watercourses.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a damp-proof course in masonry?
options: To increase the mortar strength
To resist moisture passing through the construction
To make the wall easier to paint
To replace wall ties
questions.explanation: A correctly placed DPC forms a barrier to moisture movement.

questions.prompt: Why are weep vents provided above a cavity tray?
options: To hold insulation in place
To allow collected moisture to drain to the outside
To strengthen the lintel
To ventilate the room
questions.explanation: Weeps provide a discharge route for water intercepted by the tray.

questions.prompt: How should a cavity wall tie normally be installed?
options: Sloping down toward the inner leaf
To the specified spacing and orientation, with the drip positioned to prevent water crossing
Touching the back of the outer leaf only
Bent around insulation wherever convenient
questions.explanation: Tie type, spacing, embedment and orientation must follow the design and manufacturer's requirements.

questions.prompt: What is the main reason for maintaining the specified lap in bonded brickwork?
options: To reduce the number of perpends
To avoid continuous vertical joints and achieve the intended bond
To make every course a soldier course
To remove the need for line and level checks
questions.explanation: Correct lap prevents stacked perpends and maintains the specified bond.

questions.prompt: What is a gauge rod used for when setting out masonry?
options: Checking electrical voltage
Transferring and checking course heights and vertical features
Measuring mortar strength
Cleaning the cavity
questions.explanation: A gauge rod helps keep course heights and related features consistent.

questions.prompt: Which check best confirms that a rectangular opening is square?
options: Measure only its width
Compare the two diagonal measurements
Count the bricks in one jamb
Check only the first course
questions.explanation: Equal diagonals are a useful check that a rectangle is square.

questions.prompt: Where should the required mortar mix and proportions be confirmed?
options: From colour alone
From the current specification or approved mix information
From whichever mix was used on the last job
By adding cement until it feels stiff
questions.explanation: The specified mix must be followed rather than guessed from appearance.

questions.prompt: Frost is forecast before fresh masonry has cured. What is the correct response?
options: Add unapproved antifreeze
Follow the cold-weather method and protect or postpone the work as required
Soak the wall with water
Remove all joint finishes
questions.explanation: Fresh masonry must be protected using the approved cold-weather arrangements.

questions.prompt: Why is a movement joint included in a masonry elevation?
options: To replace a DPC
To accommodate designed movement and reduce uncontrolled cracking
To carry wall ties
To make the wall permanently rigid
questions.explanation: Movement joints allow expected expansion, contraction or other movement at designed locations.

questions.prompt: Why should mortar droppings be kept clear of the cavity?
options: They improve insulation
They can bridge moisture and obstruct cavity components
They make ties easier to see
They increase ventilation
questions.explanation: A clean cavity helps prevent moisture bridging and allows components to work as designed.

questions.prompt: In a soldier course, how are the bricks normally oriented?
options: Laid flat with the long face horizontal
Set vertically on end with the narrow face showing
Placed diagonally through the cavity
Laid as headers in every leaf
questions.explanation: A soldier course uses bricks standing vertically, subject to the drawing and specification.

questions.prompt: What gives the most reliable line for a wall with a raking cut?
options: Cut each unit by eye
Set out the rake from the drawing and use a controlled template or line
Make the final course level
Increase every bed joint randomly
questions.explanation: Accurate set-out and a consistent guide keep the rake to the required line.

questions.prompt: Before replacing a damaged brick, what should be established?
options: Only the nearest merchant
The cause, the approved repair method and a compatible replacement
That the new brick is the brightest colour
That all surrounding mortar can be removed at once
questions.explanation: A repair should address the cause and use a compatible method and material.

questions.prompt: A drawing quantity is calculated before ordering bricks. What should be added where the project information requires it?
options: An arbitrary amount
The specified allowance for cuts, damage and waste
A second full order
Nothing under any circumstances
questions.explanation: A justified waste allowance helps provide enough material without excessive over-ordering.

questions.prompt: A figured dimension conflicts with a measurement scaled from the drawing. What should you do?
options: Use the scaled measurement
Stop and seek clarification using the project procedure
Average the two values
Change the drawing
questions.explanation: Conflicting information must be clarified; drawings should not be altered or guessed.

questions.prompt: When should a mortar joint normally be finished?
options: At a consistent stage when the mortar is firm enough to form the specified profile
Only after the wall is painted
While the mortar is running wet
After the scaffold is removed
questions.explanation: Consistent timing helps produce the specified profile without smearing or tearing the mortar.

questions.prompt: A delivery will block another trade's access. What is the best action?
options: Say nothing until it arrives
Coordinate the timing and access with the relevant people
Move their materials without permission
Cancel the delivery yourself
questions.explanation: Early, clear coordination helps the wider build team work safely and efficiently.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour supports an inclusive site culture?
options: Using unwanted nicknames
Listening respectfully and challenging inappropriate behaviour through the correct route
Excluding new starters from briefings
Sharing personal information as a joke
questions.explanation: Respectful communication and appropriate challenge support inclusion and dignity at work.

questions.prompt: A colleague says they are struggling and it is affecting safe work. What is the best first response?
options: Tell everyone on site
Listen, encourage appropriate support and follow the site's safety arrangements
Ignore it because it is private
Give medical advice
questions.explanation: Support should be respectful, confidential where possible and linked to suitable workplace or professional help.

questions.prompt: What should be done with a damaged bricklaying hand tool?
options: Keep using it until the shift ends
Remove it from use and repair or replace it through the correct procedure
Hide the defect with tape
Lend it to another operative
questions.explanation: Damaged tools should not remain in use because they can cause poor work or injury.
